forbidden_values._doc: THE CONCEPT THE PREVIOUS SNAPSHOT LACKED ENTIRELY. Assertions are STRUCTURAL — a path plus a predicate — never a string ban on the serialized body. That is not a style preference: $299 CANNOT be string-banned, because it is simultaneously Pro's retired priceUsdAnnual and Enterprise's live priceUsdMonthly, which is why ops/forbidden-phrases.json deliberately leaves it un-enumerated and says so in its own bare_token_reason. A structural assertion names WHERE the value may not appear, so it stays correct when the figure changes.
forbidden_values.enforced_by: scripts/check-served-surface-values.mjs (SERVED_SURFACE_VALUES_VERDICT), offline mode, fail-closed in deploy.yml

assertions.reason: brand-facts.md:552 — "$299/mo as an Enterprise list price" is a HIGH-severity forbidden phrase; :143 — Enterprise no longer publishes a price. null is a REFUSAL, never 0 and never "free".
brand-facts.md:134 gives Enterprise monthly quota as `custom`. Publishing 100000 also made Enterprise indistinguishable from Pro on the public ladder. license.ts keeps enforcing 100,000.

THE OTHER DIRECTION, and it is not optional. Without it the whole contract is satisfiable by an endpoint that nulls every price — a gate that only bans values passes hardest when the surface is broken.
The refusal is a VALUE change, never a key removal. A consumer asserting the six-key set must be unaffected; omitting the key instead of nulling it would break them.

ADDITIVE, in both directions. The API pair must stay: every API consumer reads it, and the Telegram bot falls back to it against an older server. The per-surface telegram block must be present: the bot reads free.telegram.monthly_alerts as its allowance. Removing either is a breaking change, never a tidy-up. The path resolves on the pre-fix captured body too (free exists there), so --prove-catches-ch1 still evaluates every assertion; that body now yields one more violation (no telegram key) and the current body none.

free_telegram_note: free.telegram is the Telegram bot's own allowance, in the bot's own unit: a DELIVERED ALERT (a silent HOLD costs nothing), where the API meters a returned verdict. The bot stamps each 30-day window with the allowance it opened under and serves max(stamp, monthly_alerts) while that window is open, so a change to this figure never walls a chat mid-window. daily_alerts is a real cap but, against a 100-alert month, binds only for a chat whose monthly allowance is above it (a referral bonus, or a window opened under the old figure); Telegram copy states it only where that is material. Never quote this figure on an API surface, or the API's figure on a Telegram one.
price_usd_6month_note: 🛑 TWO PROPERTIES, both load-bearing. (1) null is a REFUSAL — 'not sold on this term' — exactly as daily_calls' null is. It is never 0 and never a scaled monthly: plans.ts::planPrepayTotalUsd already refuses to fabricate a term nobody priced, and this field is that refusal projected onto the wire. A consumer coercing enterprise's null to 0 would advertise a free plan. (2) It is a TOTAL, not a monthly rate: 39.9 is what the card is charged once, for six months. A consumer rendering it beside price_usd MUST say which ('$39.90/6mo'), or the pair reads as a price cut. The endpoint projects it through planPrepayTotalUsd rather than reading plan.priceUsd6Month directly, so the 'never fabricate an unpriced term' decision has exactly ONE derivation. Both properties are pinned in tests/plans-public-api.test.ts and both were proven able to fail — see proven_able_to_fail.
null_daily_calls_note: enterprise.daily_calls is null, and null is a REFUSAL — not 'unlimited' and not zero. src/lib/plans.ts::planDailyCallsLabel carries the same warning for the copy path: no real Enterprise deal has set a daily cap, so a consumer must render the ABSENCE rather than substitute a number or the word 'unlimited', which PRICING-FLAT-CALL-BILLING-AND-6MONTH-W1 R-E removed from this ladder. A consumer that coerces null to 0 would refuse every Enterprise call; one that reads it as unlimited would publish a claim no contract supports. Pinned by tests/plans-public-api.test.ts.
null_price_usd_note: 🛑 enterprise.price_usd and enterprise.monthly_calls are null, and null is a REFUSAL — "custom, ask us" — never zero, never "free", never unlimited. This is the SAME refusal daily_calls and price_usd_6month already carried on this rung, so a nulled value was already in the wire format every consumer handles. A consumer must OMIT the figure; rendering "null" or substituting a number is the defect this snapshot records the end of.
generated_at_note: 🛑 generated_at is a RENDER STAMP, not a producer-freshness signal, and it is the ONLY per-request-varying field in the body. verification-gates.md — 'freshness alarms measure PRODUCERS, never rendered artifacts' — so no canary may key staleness on it: it reports the serving process's clock, not the ladder's cadence. The ladder changes only on deploy, and the container restart is its real invalidation boundary. It is emitted so a machine consumer can tell when a cached copy was minted, and it is documented here so a future freshness check does not mistake it for a producer stamp.
algovault_block_note: _algovault IS on the ALLOW-list, ratified by Mr.1 2026-08-27 (Q3=b). src/lib/public-cta.ts declares that any public JSON endpoint merges buildPublicCtaBlock(), and audits/public-cta-shape-snapshot-2026-07-15.json lists _algovault plus these four sub-keys under each adopting endpoint's allowed_keys. The block is an exported pure formatter returning static approved copy — no I/O, no live figures — so it changes neither the cost profile nor the cacheability of a static projection. Unchanged by this wave.
error_contract: No error path exists. buildPublicPlansBody() is total: it reads module-level constants and a frozen record, calls one pure total helper (planPrepayTotalUsd, which returns null rather than throwing on an unpriced term), performs no I/O, and cannot throw on any input — the route takes no parameters. There is no 4xx and no 5xx branch. An unreachable endpoint is an infrastructure fault, not an application state, and must be diagnosed as one.
auth_contract: UNAUTHENTICATED by design, unlike its register-site neighbours /api/bot/validate-key, /api/entitlement/* and /api/ops/build. The consumer this exists for is a FREE, unlinked Telegram chat, which holds no api_key and no internal key. Every field served is already public copy on algovault.com/#pricing and on the /signup plan cards. Adding auth here would recreate the exact gap the endpoint closes.

cache_contract.description: Cache-Control: public, max-age=300. No in-process cache: the handler is a pure projection with no DB touch, so caching it in-process would add an invalidation problem to a function that has none. The 300s TTL matches the bot's EXISTING five-minute entitlement-drain cadence (the ladder mirror rides that cron — no new schedule), so the mirror can never be more than one drain cycle behind an edge copy. UNCHANGED by this wave: an additive field does not move the invalidation boundary.
cache_contract.staleness_signal: NONE, deliberately. The ladder changes only on deploy and the container restart is the invalidation boundary. Do not key a freshness alarm on generated_at — see generated_at_note.

drift_check._doc: REPLACES drift_check_command, which was a SHELL STRING IN A JSON FIELD. git grep for this snapshot family outside audits/ returned ZERO hits: it was in no script, no workflow and no cron, so it had never once run. Prose in a JSON field is not a control — the Completeness Standard says a rule that has failed as prose must become a gate or be deleted. It is now a named, executable script with a verdict token.

drift_check.note: The OFFLINE mode is the gate. The projection is a pure function, so this class is catchable deterministically at build time and does not need the network. The live mode catches host/deploy drift the build cannot see. Neither substitutes for the other, and the live one must never be the only enforcement.
